How many band changes are measurement error?

Source: R/state.R
wgh_false_moves.Rd

Measurement error moves children across band cut-offs without any change in growth. This function measures how much. It redraws each measured height from the error-free height with a chosen measurement error SD, rounds it to one decimal as a school scale would, recomputes HAZ with the WHO reference, assigns bands and pairs consecutive visits, exactly as wgh_states() and wgh_transitions() do. It then compares the measured transitions with the error-free ones. Repeating this for several error SDs shows how fast false transitions grow with measurement error (Book 2 Chapter 12).

Usage

wgh_false_moves(
  x,
  error_sds = c(0.5, 1, 1.5),
  percentiles = c(10, 25, 75, 90),
  min_interval = 0.5,
  max_interval = 2.5,
  attended_only = TRUE,
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

x

A wgh_sim object from wgh_simulate(), or growth data with id (or pid), sex, age, height and optionally height_true.

error_sds

Measurement error SDs in cm to try.

percentiles, min_interval, max_interval

Band cut-offs and the allowed interval between visits, as in wgh_states() and wgh_transitions().

attended_only

For a wgh_sim object, use only the visits that were attended (the observed visit schedule).

seed

Random seed for the redrawn measurement error.

Value

A tibble with one row per error SD: n_transitions, persistence_pct (measured band unchanged), observed_moves_pct (measured band changed), false_moves_pct (share of measured changes in which the error-free band did not change) and missed_moves_pct (share of error-free changes not seen in the measured bands). Attribute "by_band" gives the false moves by starting band.

Details

With simulated data the error-free height is known (height_true in the truth file of a wgh_simulate() object). With real data it is not, and the observed height is used as the reference: the result then shows how many additional band changes a given amount of extra measurement error would create, which is a lower bound for the real share.

Next steps

Report the expected share of false moves with any transition analysis (wgh_transition_matrix(), wgh_canalization_summary()), use wgh_rtm() to separate regression to the mean from real catch-up, and wgh_hmm() to model misclassification directly.

Examples

sim <- wgh_simulate(3000, seed = 3)
fm <- wgh_false_moves(sim, error_sds = c(0.5, 1, 1.5))
fm
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   error_sd_cm n_transitions persistence_pct observed_moves_pct false_moves_pct
#>         <dbl>         <int>           <dbl>              <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1         0.5          3697            78.0               22.0            36.1
#> 2         1            3697            71.7               28.3            55.9
#> 3         1.5          3697            65.3               34.7            64.1
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: missed_moves_pct <dbl>
attr(fm, "by_band")
#> # A tibble: 15 × 5
#>    error_sd_cm from_band n_transitions observed_moves_pct false_moves_pct
#>          <dbl> <fct>             <int>              <dbl>           <dbl>
#>  1         0.5 Very low            154               40.9            39.7
#>  2         1   Very low            158               41.8            48.5
#>  3         1.5 Very low            170               50.6            64.0
#>  4         0.5 Low                 348               37.9            42.4
#>  5         1   Low                 369               47.7            67.0
#>  6         1.5 Low                 388               55.9            70.5
#>  7         0.5 Middle             2033               14.4            35.6
#>  8         1   Middle             2010               18.1            49.0
#>  9         1.5 Middle             1942               23.6            59.5
#> 10         0.5 High                710               33.0            34.6
#> 11         1   High                705               44.4            58.5
#> 12         1.5 High                710               50.8            66.8
#> 13         0.5 Very high           452               20.8            29.8
#> 14         1   Very high           455               28.1            57.8
#> 15         1.5 Very high           487               33.1            62.7
# Real data: extra error on top of the recorded heights
wgh_false_moves(growdat, error_sds = c(0.5, 1))
#> No error-free height in the data. The recorded height is used as the reference,
#> so the shares are lower bounds.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   error_sd_cm n_transitions persistence_pct observed_moves_pct false_moves_pct
#>         <dbl>         <int>           <dbl>              <dbl>           <dbl>
